purpose: Generate a non-publishable c64-shaped control oracle after an explicit 50 ms burst-admission window, then use that frozen oracle for fresh-server determinism replays.
hypothesis: The prior 54/64 same-shape replay was caused by variable HTTP arrival-to-slot assignment. A fixed admission window should make all 64 requests visible before slot assignment and stabilize batch composition.
pilot_policy: This run exists only to freeze a deployment-shape token-ID oracle. Its throughput is diagnostic and cannot be published or used as a speed claim.
pilot_gates: 64 of 64 requests complete with 128 retained token IDs
cross-base token-ID collision count is zero
server log confirms a 50 ms settle window
no kernel, GPU, OOM, or server fault
validation_after_pilot: Freeze the pilot's 64 token-ID digests, preregister their hash, then require two fresh control servers to match 64/64 exactly. A candidate optimization remains blocked until both replays pass.
